draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Tiruvannamalai! The Arulmigu Annamalaiyar Temple sits along the Annamalai hill here, and thousands come every month for Girivalam and every year for the Karthika Deepam festival.
draft.hungryLine: Do it the Tamil way: idli or dosai with chutney and sambar for tiffin, then a strong filter coffee.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Make the Arulmigu Annamalaiyar Temple your first stop, then look up at Annamalai hill rising right behind it.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a quiet corner near Annamalai hill and just watch the pilgrims go by.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The town's legend begins on Mount Kailash, when Parvati playfully closed Shiva's eyes in a flower garden.

spots.name: Arulmigu Annamalaiyar Temple
spots.detail: In town · The great Shiva temple along Annamalai hill

spots.name: Annamalai hill
spots.detail: Right behind the temple · The hill pilgrims walk around on Girivalam

legends.title: Girivalam
legends.body: Every month, pilgrims walk around Annamalai hill in the practice called Girivalam. Thousands turn up, so you won't be walking alone.

tips.title: Plan around Karthika Deepam.
tips.body: The annual Karthika Deepam festival draws thousands, so book early or pick another time if you want it quiet.

tips.title: Dress for the temple.
tips.body: This is a major pilgrimage town, so cover shoulders and knees at Annamalaiyar.

story.title: A playful moment
story.body: The legend behind Tiruvannamalai starts with Parvati playfully closing Shiva's eyes in a flower garden atop Mount Kailash. It's one of the stories tied to the town's name.

story.title: A municipality
story.body: Tiruvannamalai Municipality was set up in 1886. Today it's run as the Tiruvanamalai City Municipal Corporation.

story.title: Pilgrim city
story.body: The city is a Hindu cultural hub, with retail, resorts and spinning mills too. It's about 150 km from Chennai and 145 km from Bengaluru by road and rail.
